sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: It is September 1579.
sentences.zh: 现在是1579年9月。

sentences.en: We are in the sump of sin.
sentences.zh: 我们身处罪恶的汇聚地。

sentences.en: We are in Rome itself.
sentences.zh: 我们就在罗马城内。

sentences.en: And we're at a dinner in a place called the English College.
sentences.zh: 我们正在一个叫英国学院的地方参加晚宴。

sentences.en: And this is a seminary where English students can train for the Catholic priesthood.
sentences.zh: 这是一所神学院，英国学生可以在这里接受天主教神职培训。

sentences.en: And the guest of honour at this dinner is a man who Francis Walsingham, spymaster to Elizabeth I, regards as his most dangerous enemy, putting on one side, Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 晚宴的贵宾是弗朗西斯·沃尔辛厄姆（伊丽莎白一世的间谍头子）眼中最危险的敌人，当然，苏格兰女王玛丽除外。

sentences.en: And the name of this man is William Allen.
sentences.zh: 这个人的名字叫威廉·艾伦。

sentences.en: He is a Catholic prieSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位天主教神父。

sentences.en: He is a scholar.
sentences.zh: 他是一位学者。

sentences.en: And like the co-founder of Goalhanger, Tony Pasta, he is a man of Lancashire.
sentences.zh: 而且像Goalhanger的联合创始人托尼·帕斯塔一样，他是兰开夏郡人。

sentences.en: So a man of Lancashire, educated at Oxford.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是兰开夏郡人，在牛津受过教育。

sentences.en: So he's very like Tony Pasta.
sentences.zh: 所以他很像托尼·帕斯塔。

sentences.en: Well, in some ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某些方面是这样。

sentences.en: Listeners can tell straight away that this is going to be a very bad man.
sentences.zh: 听众马上就能听出来，这肯定是个大坏蛋。

sentences.en: Tell us about William Allen and why he's such a bad man, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，给我们讲讲威廉·艾伦，为什么他是个大坏蛋。

sentences.en: He's got a mole, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他有颗痣，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got a mole.
sentences.zh: 他有颗痣。

sentences.en: He's got a reddish beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着红褐色的胡子。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all stacking up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些特征都凑齐了。

sentences.en: He's very tall.
sentences.zh: 他个子很高。

sentences.en: He's very slim.
sentences.zh: 他很瘦。

sentences.en: He's in his late 40s.
sentences.zh: 他四十多岁。

sentences.en: And as you said, he'd been a brilliant student at Oxford.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他曾是牛津大学的优等生。

sentences.en: Then he'd been a fellow at Oriel College.
sentences.zh: 后来成了奥里尔学院的院士。

sentences.en: So a glittering academic career there.
sentences.zh: 所以他有着辉煌的学术生涯。

sentences.en: But because he's a very devout Catholic, when Elizabeth comes in and establishes the Protestant settlement, he can't put up with it.
sentences.zh: 但因为他是一位非常虔诚的天主教徒，当伊丽莎白上台并建立新教体制时，他无法忍受。

sentences.en: And so he leaves England and goes into permanent exile.
sentences.zh: 于是他离开英格兰，开始了永久流亡。

sentences.en: And when he's in exile, he sets up seminaries with the aim of training English Catholic priests who can then be sent back to England.
sentences.zh: 流亡期间，他建立了神学院，旨在培养可以被送回英格兰的英国天主教神父。

sentences.en: And the first of these seminaries he sets up at Dowie in the Low Countries and the second one at Reims in France.
sentences.zh: 他建立的第一所神学院在低地国家的杜埃，第二所在法国的兰斯。

sentences.en: So you were asking, you know, how are people in England being kept abreast of all these developments?
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才问，英格兰的人们是如何了解所有这些进展的？

sentences.en: It's these priests who are being sent by, trained and sent by William Allen to England.
sentences.zh: 就是通过这些由威廉·艾伦培训并派往英格兰的神父。

sentences.en: Their aim is to kind of keep alive the flame of recusancy in England,
sentences.zh: 他们的目的是在英格兰维持天主教信仰的火种，

sentences.en: to give mass to Catholics and to succor them and to let them know that they haven't been abandoned by the Catholic powers of Europe.
sentences.zh: 为天主教徒举行弥撒，给予他们援助，并让他们知道欧洲的天主教势力并没有抛弃他们。

sentences.en: But also, if they can, to try and to make conversions.
sentences.zh: 但如果可能的话，他们也试图进行传教。

sentences.en: So I guess, you know, again, pursuing the kind of Cold War analogy, KGB agents in Britain, they were kind of there to establish links with pre-existing communists,
sentences.zh: 我想，再次用冷战类比的话，就像英国的克格勃特工，他们一方面是为了与现有的共产主义者建立联系，

sentences.en: but also to recruit agents, say, in, you know, Cambridge or the civil service or whatever.
sentences.zh: 另一方面也是为了在剑桥或公务员队伍等地方招募特工。

sentences.en: And so these priests have been going to England, obviously, it's incredibly dangerous, but they come in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以这些神父一直潜入英格兰，这显然极其危险，但他们人数众多。

sentences.en: So the first four priests sent by Allen had arrived in England in 1574 and more had followed over the succeeding year.
sentences.zh: 艾伦派出的首批四名神父于1574年抵达英格兰，随后几年又有更多人跟进。

sentences.en: So by 1579, Allen has around 100 priests kind of working undercover in England, working to keep the flame of Catholicism alive.
sentences.zh: 因此到1579年，艾伦在英格兰有大约100名神父在秘密工作，努力维持天主教的火种。

sentences.en: But now, you know, he's come to Rome to hold this dinner because he wants to turbocharge this mission.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他来到罗马举行这次晚宴，是因为他想为这项使命注入强心剂。

sentences.en: And he's come to Rome because he wants the Pope's personal backing for the acceleration of this mission.
sentences.zh: 他来到罗马是因为他想要教皇的个人支持，以加速这项使命。

sentences.en: And nine days before this dinner with which we opened the second half, he'd had an interview with the Pope and the Pope had given the green light,
sentences.zh: 在我们下半场开篇提到的那次晚宴的九天前，他曾与教皇会面，教皇开了绿灯，

sentences.en: had given his blessing to this great project.
sentences.zh: 并为这个伟大的计划给予了祝福。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Allen is a brilliant networker, very, very skilled in the arts of diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，艾伦是一位出色的联络人，在外交艺术方面非常、非常有技巧。

sentences.en: He's been assiduous in fostering close links with Philip II of Spain and has actually persuaded him to sponsor an invasion of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他一直勤勉地与西班牙国王腓力二世建立密切联系，并成功说服他资助一场对爱尔兰的入侵。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth is the Queen of England and Wales, but she is also the Queen of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白不仅是英格兰和威尔士的女王，也是爱尔兰的女王。

sentences.en: So this is an invasion of her backyard.
sentences.zh: 所以，这等于是入侵了她的后院。

sentences.en: And that evening at dinner, the dinner being held in Rome in mid-September 1579, Allen gives his fellow guests the great news.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，在1579年9月中旬于罗马举行的晚宴上，艾伦向他的客人们宣布了这个大好消息。

sentences.en: You know, the Pope is on board.
sentences.zh: 你知道，教皇支持我们。

sentences.en: He's given us more funding.
sentences.zh: 他给了我们更多的资金。

sentences.en: An invasion force with Spanish soldiers has landed in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 一支由西班牙士兵组成的入侵部队已经在爱尔兰登陆了。

sentences.en: It's all great.
sentences.zh: 一切都很棒。

sentences.en: It's all kicking off.
sentences.zh: 一切都开始了。

sentences.en: Things are really, really looking up.
sentences.zh: 事情真的、真的在好转。

sentences.en: And Stephen Alford wrote a brilliant book about the kind of the espionage war called The Watchers.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·阿尔福德写了一本关于这种间谍战的精彩著作，书名叫《守望者》。

sentences.en: Yeah, The Watchers.
sentences.zh: 没错，《守望者》。

sentences.en: Great book.
sentences.zh: 很棒的书。

sentences.en: He describes the speech that Allen gave.
sentences.zh: 他描述了艾伦发表的那场演讲。

sentences.en: It must have been extraordinary and moving, revealing his persuasive power to inspire and to motivate, which no one ever doubts.
sentences.zh: 那一定非同寻常且感人至深，展现了他那无人质疑的、鼓舞和激励人心的说服力。

sentences.en: I mean, that's why Walsingham sees him as such a dangerous foe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是为什么沃尔辛厄姆视他为如此危险的敌人。

sentences.en: And six priests sign up to the mission to England that very evening.
sentences.zh: 就在那天晚上，有六名神父报名参加了前往英格兰的任务。

sentences.en: And Allen says, you will be going to England in, you know, just a few months at the start of 1580.
sentences.zh: 艾伦说，你们将在几个月后，也就是1580年初前往英格兰。

sentences.en: So that's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: There are those six priests, but there is also another priest there who needs no encouragement whatsoever to plan for a mission to England.
sentences.zh: 除了那六名神父，还有另一位神父在场，他根本不需要任何鼓励就计划着前往英格兰的任务。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Robert Persons, who is in his early 30s.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫罗伯特·帕森斯，三十出头。

sentences.en: And like you, Dominic, he is a Balian man.
sentences.zh: 而且像你一样，多米尼克，他是个巴利安人。

sentences.en: And like you, he is bold, formidable and charismatic.
sentences.zh: 而且像你一样，他大胆、令人生畏且富有魅力。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: Unlike you, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，和你不同的是。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 没错，他是个神父。

sentences.en: He's a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 他是个神父。

sentences.en: He'd been ordained a priest only the year before.
sentences.zh: 他前一年才刚刚被祝圣为神父。

sentences.en: And not just any kind of priest, because specifically he had been ordained a priest of the Society of Jesus.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是普通的神父，他特别被祝圣为耶稣会的神父。

sentences.en: So shorthand, a Jesuit.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就是耶稣会士。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So tell us a little bit about the Jesuits, because they are, they're about 40 years old at this point, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲耶稣会士吧，因为他们此时成立大约40年了，对吧？

sentences.en: They're a religious order.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个宗教修会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Poverty, chastity, obedience.
sentences.zh: 守贫、守贞、服从。

sentences.en: But what marks them out is this kind of fanatical loyalty to the Pope, right?
sentences.zh: 但让他们与众不同的是那种对教皇的狂热忠诚，对吧？

sentences.en: Fanatical devotion to the Pope, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信是对教皇的狂热奉献。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Monty Python would put it.
sentences.zh: 就像蒙提·派森会说的那样。

sentences.en: They are the kind of the shock troops who have been formed to combat the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 他们是为对抗宗教改革而组建的突击部队。

sentences.en: And their vocation is to win souls for Christ in this last era of a declining and grasping world.
sentences.zh: 他们的使命是在这个衰落且贪婪的世界的最后时代，为基督赢得灵魂。

sentences.en: And so they've traveled to the limits of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们已经走到了世界的尽头。

sentences.en: You know, they've gone to China.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们去了中国。

sentences.en: They go to Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们去了日本。

sentences.en: People have seen Shogun.
sentences.zh: 人们看过《幕府将军》吧。

sentences.en: The priests in that are Jesuits.
sentences.zh: 里面的神父就是耶稣会士。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But persons who is English, he thinks, yeah, I mean, it's great sending priests off to China and Japan, but there's an obvious place where we need to make conversions.
sentences.zh: 但是身为英国人的帕森斯认为，是的，派神父去中国和日本固然很好，但有一个显而易见的地方我们需要去传教。

sentences.en: And this is my own native land, England.
sentences.zh: 那就是我的祖国，英格兰。

sentences.en: And so he has been pushing for this ever since he's become a Jesuit, so the whole year since his ordination.
sentences.zh: 所以自从他成为耶稣会士以来，也就是他受戒后的整整一年里，他一直在推动这件事。

sentences.en: And his superior, the Jesuit general, is reluctant because he doesn't really want to embroil the order in a mission that will be both very perilous and very controversial.
sentences.zh: 而他的上级，耶稣会总会长，对此很勉强，因为他真的不想让修会卷入一场既危险又充满争议的任务中。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is kind of plunging your hand into the magic mix.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的就像把手伸进魔法混合物里一样。

sentences.en: But persons is very, very determined.
sentences.zh: 但帕森斯非常、非常坚定。

sentences.en: And so he has joined forces with Alan, and the pair of them have been pushing for this kind of great mission to England.
sentences.zh: 所以他与艾伦联手，两人一直在推动这场前往英格兰的伟大任务。

sentences.en: And Alan is very keen.
sentences.zh: 艾伦非常热心。

sentences.en: You know, he welcomes persons with open arms because he kind of admires them as the, you know, the spiritual elite of the counter-reformation, the kind of the very sharpest edge.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他张开双臂欢迎帕森斯，因为他钦佩他们作为反宗教改革的精神精英，那种最锋利的刀刃。

sentences.en: And so over the next few months after this dinner, Alan and persons refine their plans, and the Pope gives them more funds.
sentences.zh: 所以在这次晚宴后的几个月里，艾伦和帕森斯完善了他们的计划，教皇也给了他们更多的资金。

sentences.en: And secret documents are drawn up detailing lists of English Catholics who are in exile, and so therefore readily contactable,
sentences.zh: 秘密文件被起草，详细列出了流亡在外的英国天主教徒名单，因此很容易联系到他们，

sentences.en: and who are ready to join the King of Spain in an invasion of England.
sentences.zh: 并且他们已经准备好加入西班牙国王的行列，入侵英格兰。

sentences.en: And the conspirators, when they discuss this plot, they talk very openly, because they know that they're among friends, that there are no kind of listeners eavesdropping.
sentences.zh: 阴谋家们在讨论这个阴谋时，谈话非常公开，因为他们知道自己身处朋友之中，没有人在窃听。

sentences.en: They talk openly of the joy that they would feel at seeing, and I quote, the Spaniards, Lords of England, and Elizabeth Tudor, Mistress Bess, as they call her,
sentences.zh: 他们公开谈论看到——我引用一下——“西班牙人成为英格兰的主人，而伊丽莎白·都铎，贝丝夫人，正如他们所称呼的那样，

sentences.en: shaked of her estate.
sentences.zh: 被剥夺了她的领地”时所感到的快乐。

sentences.en: And William Allen leaves Rome with this kind of band of priests, this kind of shock force of undercover agents who will be crossing into England.
sentences.zh: 威廉·艾伦带着这群神父离开了罗马，这支潜伏特工的突击部队即将进入英格兰。

sentences.en: They leave Rome on the 25th of February, 1580.
sentences.zh: 他们于1580年2月25日离开罗马。

sentences.en: So it is all kicking off.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都开始了。

sentences.en: But there is a particular man with them, isn't there, who listeners might want to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 但他们中间有一个特别的人，不是吗？听众们可能需要注意一下。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Charles Sled, who has come along as a kind of fixer and a courier for them.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫查尔斯·斯莱德，他作为他们的联络员和信使随行。

sentences.en: And he's a sort of nondescript man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个相貌平平的人。

sentences.en: He's literate.
sentences.zh: 他识字。

sentences.en: He's very effective.
sentences.zh: 他非常能干。

sentences.en: He was once an apprentice to a merchant.
sentences.zh: 他曾经是一名商人的学徒。

sentences.en: He had been in Rome since the previous summer.
sentences.zh: 他从前一个夏天起就一直待在罗马。

sentences.en: He had gone to St. Peter's for confession.
sentences.zh: 他曾去圣彼得大教堂忏悔。

sentences.en: And then he'd begun working as a servant for an English Catholic churchman in Rome.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始在罗马为一位英国天主教神职人员当仆人。

sentences.en: And how has he got involved?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么卷进来的？

sentences.en: How has he got involved with this party?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么加入这个团体的？

sentences.en: Why is he with them?
sentences.zh: 他为什么和他们在一起？

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's in his mid-20s.
sentences.zh: 是的，他二十多岁。

sentences.en: He's English.
sentences.zh: 他是英国人。

sentences.en: He's come to Rome because he's a Catholic, or so he says.
sentences.zh: 他来到罗马是因为他是天主教徒，或者他是这么说的。

sentences.en: And he's taken confession, which demonstrates that he must be a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他进行了忏悔，这证明他一定是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: And so as an English Catholic, he's looking around for a job.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名英国天主教徒，他在找工作。

sentences.en: And he gets his job with an English churchman in Rome.
sentences.zh: 他在罗马为一位英国神职人员找到了工作。

sentences.en: And that means that when this English churchman hosts dinners, Charles Sled is in attendance.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当这位英国神职人员举办晚宴时，查尔斯·斯莱德就在场。

sentences.en: And William Allen and Robert Persons are regular attendees at these dinners.
sentences.zh: 威廉·艾伦和罗伯特·帕森斯是这些晚宴的常客。

sentences.en: And Sled is there, you know, kind of like a waiter.
sentences.zh: 斯莱德就在那里，你知道，就像个服务员。

sentences.en: He's kind of hovering with the wine.
sentences.zh: 他端着酒徘徊。

sentences.en: No one's paying any attention to him.
sentences.zh: 没人注意他。

sentences.en: But of course, he can listen to everything that is being said.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他可以听到所说的一切。

sentences.en: And Allen does spot him and realizes that he's kind of very able.
sentences.zh: 艾伦确实注意到了他，并意识到他非常有能力。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got all the qualities that you would want in a good servant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他具备了优秀仆人所应有的一切品质。

sentences.en: And so when Allen heads off with the Jesuits from Rome bound for England,
sentences.zh: 所以当艾伦带着耶稣会士从罗马出发前往英格兰时，

sentences.en: Sled goes with them and often is riding ahead of them to fix rooms and to take letters for Allen and things like that.
sentences.zh: 斯莱德也随行，并且经常骑马走在他们前面，去安排房间、为艾伦送信等等。

sentences.en: So by the 6th of April, before Allen arrives in Paris, Sled is already there.
sentences.zh: 所以到4月6日，在艾伦抵达巴黎之前，斯莱德就已经在那里了。

sentences.en: And then soon afterwards, he's in Reims, which is, of course, home of one of the two seminaries set up by Allen.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他出现在兰斯，那里当然是艾伦建立的两所神学院之一的所在地。

sentences.en: And then shortly after that, he pops up in Rouen, which is one of the main centers of English Catholic exiles in France.
sentences.zh: 此后不久，他又出现在鲁昂，那是法国英国天主教流亡者的主要中心之一。

sentences.en: And everywhere he goes, he's carrying letters from Allen.
sentences.zh: 无论他走到哪里，他都带着艾伦的信件。

sentences.en: And then he's taking letters back to Allen and the fellow conspirators.
sentences.zh: 然后他把信带回给艾伦和其他阴谋同伙。

sentences.en: And he is attending their meetings.
sentences.zh: 他参加了他们的会议。

sentences.en: You know, he's laying the table.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他摆放餐桌。

sentences.en: He's pouring the wine.
sentences.zh: 他倒酒。

sentences.en: He's serving the food.
sentences.zh: 他上菜。

sentences.en: And he's listening to their homilies.
sentences.zh: 他听着他们的布道。

sentences.en: And he's listening to all the details of their conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 他听着他们阴谋的所有细节。

sentences.en: And he's a tremendous fellow to have around.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常了不起的随行人员。

sentences.en: And what a blessing it is for William Allen and the Jesuits and the various priests to have him on hand.
sentences.zh: 对于威廉·艾伦、耶稣会士和各位神父来说，有他在身边真是太幸运了。

sentences.en: And then abruptly in mid-May, Sled vanishes.
sentences.zh: 然后，5月中旬，斯莱德突然消失了。

sentences.en: And people may be wondering, where has he gone, this trusted servant of William Allen?
sentences.zh: 人们可能在想，这个威廉·艾伦信任的仆人去哪了？

sentences.en: And I think that the answer to anyone who has read Le Carré will come as no surprise whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我想对于任何读过勒卡雷作品的人来说，答案一点也不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Because on the afternoon of 17th of May, he pops up in London at the court in Westminster.
sentences.zh: 因为在5月17日下午，他出现在伦敦威斯敏斯特的宫廷里。

sentences.en: And at the court in Westminster, Charles Sled, if that was indeed his name, is ushered into the presence of Francis Walsingham.
sentences.zh: 在威斯敏斯特的宫廷里，查尔斯·斯莱德（如果这确实是他的名字）被带到了弗朗西斯·沃尔辛厄姆的面前。

sentences.en: I mean, listeners must have heard this coming when they heard you talking about his eye for detail.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当听众听到你谈论他敏锐的观察力时，一定猜到了这一点。

sentences.en: And he's a brilliant master of recall.
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的记忆大师。

sentences.en: And he can keep a secret and all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他能保守秘密，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And effectively, what he now does is he hands over to Francis Walsingham all the details, all the inside dope on Allen and the Jesuit operation.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他现在所做的就是把关于艾伦和耶稣会行动的所有细节、所有内幕消息都交给了弗朗西斯·沃尔辛厄姆。

sentences.en: So he's got lists of names, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他有名单，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got, what, 300 English Catholic names on this list?
sentences.zh: 他有，什么，300个英国天主教徒的名字在名单上？

sentences.en: These are people on whom Allen said, we can rely, we can contact these people.
sentences.zh: 这些人是艾伦说我们可以依赖、可以联系的人。

sentences.en: And Sled just gives all this to Francis Walsingham.
sentences.zh: 斯莱德把这一切都给了弗朗西斯·沃尔辛厄姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's details of the pensions they're getting from the Pope.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有他们从教皇那里获得的养老金的细节。

sentences.en: And also very, very vivid physical descriptions.
sentences.zh: 以及非常、非常生动的体貌特征描述。

sentences.en: And Stephen Alford in The Watchers, which is absolutely, I mean, it's such a brilliant book.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·阿尔福德在《守望者》中写道，这本书绝对是，我的意思是，太精彩了。

sentences.en: So gripping.
sentences.zh: 非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: He describes this list as the most complete reference work then available on Queen Elizabeth's enemies.
sentences.zh: 他将这份名单描述为当时关于伊丽莎白女王敌人最完整的参考资料。

sentences.en: So it's like downloading a massive database and then uploading it so that you know all your enemy agents that you're up againSt.
sentences.zh: 这就像下载了一个庞大的数据库，然后上传它，这样你就知道你所对抗的所有敌方特工了。

sentences.en: Sort of WikiLeaks type thing.
sentences.zh: 有点像维基解密那种东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Robert Beale, so Walsingham's brother-in-law and kind of right-hand man, secretary of the Privy Council.
sentences.zh: 是的，罗伯特·比尔，也就是沃尔辛厄姆的妹夫和得力助手，枢密院秘书。

sentences.en: He writes it up and prepares it for distribution to particularly trusted members of the Privy Council.
sentences.zh: 他将其整理出来，准备分发给枢密院中特别值得信赖的成员。

sentences.en: So it's so sensitive that not everybody gets it.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常机密，不是每个人都能看到。

sentences.en: And he just titles it Priests and Seminaries Beyond the Seas.
sentences.zh: 他将其命名为《海外神父与神学院》。

sentences.en: You know, this is the key to combating these kind of enumerary agents that are coming to England.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是对抗这些进入英格兰的敌方特工的关键。

sentences.en: And this dossier, when Walsingham reads it, and he's got Sled's reports of everything that these priests have been talking about in Rome,
sentences.zh: 当沃尔辛厄姆读到这份档案时，他掌握了斯莱德关于这些神父在罗马所谈论的一切报告，

sentences.en: whether, you know, Alan was talking about Spanish invasions of Ireland and England and so on.
sentences.zh: 无论是艾伦谈论西班牙入侵爱尔兰和英格兰等等。

sentences.en: I mean, it just reinforces him in his conviction that England is at war and that the priests that Alan is sending to England might protest that they are not political agents.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这更加坚定了他认为英格兰处于战争状态的信念，艾伦派往英格兰的神父们可能会抗议说他们不是政治特工。

sentences.en: They are coming to minister to souls.
sentences.zh: 他们是来传教的。

sentences.en: But this is just equivocation.
sentences.zh: 但这只是推诿。

sentences.en: I mean, the Jesuits are notorious for equivocation among Protestants.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在抗议者眼中，耶稣会士以推诿而闻名。

sentences.en: And this is undoubtedly, I think, how Walsingham sees this kind of talk.
sentences.zh: 我认为，毫无疑问，这就是沃尔辛厄姆看待这种言论的方式。

sentences.en: Walsingham sees these priests, and the Jesuits perhaps in particular, as just arrant traitors.
sentences.zh: 沃尔辛厄姆视这些神父，尤其是耶稣会士，为彻头彻尾的叛徒。

sentences.en: They're agents of the Pope, but they're also agents of the King of Spain, who is a foreign head of state.
sentences.zh: 他们是教皇的代理人，但他们也是外国国家元首西班牙国王的代理人。

sentences.en: And they are conspiring against their anointed queen.
sentences.zh: 他们正在密谋反对他们受膏的女王。

sentences.en: So it's treason.
sentences.zh: 所以这是叛国罪。

sentences.en: So he's going to be targeting them, not for their religious beliefs, but as traitors.
sentences.zh: 所以他要针对他们，不是因为他们的宗教信仰，而是因为他们是叛徒。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this is why Elizabeth is not burning Catholics in the way that her sister had done.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么伊丽莎白没有像她姐姐那样火烧天主教徒。

sentences.en: She's learned that lesson.
sentences.zh: 她吸取了那个教训。

sentences.en: That's bad.
sentences.zh: 那很糟糕。

sentences.en: If you were up against enemies who are motivated by religious reasons, you don't condemn them for their religious reasons.
sentences.zh: 如果你面对的是出于宗教原因而行动的敌人，你不要因为他们的宗教原因而谴责他们。

sentences.en: You condemn them for treason, for being traitors to their anointed queen.
sentences.zh: 你要以叛国罪谴责他们，因为他们背叛了他们受膏的女王。

sentences.en: So for Walsingham now, it's a manhunt, right, to track down these conspirators?
sentences.zh: 所以对沃尔辛厄姆来说，现在这是一场搜捕行动，对吧，为了追捕这些阴谋分子？

sentences.en: Yeah, because he loves hunting.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为他热爱狩猎。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not a man who has much time for sport, but the sport he loves is hare coursing, so hunting hares with dogs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他并不是一个有闲暇时间去搞运动的人，但他热爱的运动是猎兔，也就是带着猎犬去追捕野兔。

sentences.en: But now, yes, basically, it's a manhunt.
sentences.zh: 但现在，是的，基本上这就是一场搜捕行动。

sentences.en: And he's got two people in particular that he's after.
sentences.zh: 而且他特别想要抓捕两个人。

sentences.en: So one of them is the Balliol man you already mentioned, Robert Persons.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是你们刚才提到的贝利奥尔学院的人，罗伯特·珀森斯。

sentences.en: And the other is Robert Persons' deputy, who is a Londoner called Edmund Campion, who ends up becoming a great hero, doesn't he, to Catholics?
sentences.zh: 另一个是罗伯特·珀森斯的副手，一个叫埃德蒙·坎皮恩的伦敦人，他最终成了天主教徒心目中的大英雄，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's a very, very impressive man.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个非常、非常令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: I mean, almost everything about him is impressive.
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于他的一切几乎都令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: So unlike William Allen, Campion had initially accepted the Protestant settlement.
sentences.zh: 所以与威廉·艾伦不同，坎皮恩最初是接受了新教的宗教和解政策的。

sentences.en: He'd gone to Oxford, where he'd been the most brilliant student of his day.
sentences.zh: 他曾就读于牛津大学，是当时最杰出的学生。

sentences.en: He had formally welcomed Elizabeth to the university, and Elizabeth had been very impressed with him.
sentences.zh: 他曾正式欢迎伊丽莎白女王访问大学，伊丽莎白对他印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: And so, too, had William Cecil, who would become Lord Burley, and had kind of adopted him as a protege.
sentences.zh: 威廉·塞西尔（即后来的伯利勋爵）也对他印象深刻，并把他当作门生来培养。

sentences.en: But Campion starts to have doubts.
sentences.zh: 但坎皮恩开始产生怀疑。

sentences.en: And in 1569, he leaves Oxford, and he goes to Dublin.
sentences.zh: 1569年，他离开牛津去了都柏林。

sentences.en: So it's part of Elizabeth's realMs.
sentences.zh: 那是伊丽莎白领土的一部分。

sentences.en: It is easier to be a Catholic there than it is in England at this point.
sentences.zh: 在当时，在那里做天主教徒比在英格兰要容易得多。

sentences.en: And he starts to embark on a process of conversion, or maybe reconversion, you should say.
sentences.zh: 他开始踏上皈依，或者说重新皈依的过程。

sentences.en: And then he ends up in Dowie, which is one of William Allen's two seminaries.
sentences.zh: 后来他到了杜埃，那是威廉·艾伦的两所神学院之一。

sentences.en: And in 1571, he's formally welcomed back into the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: 1571年，他正式重返天主教会。

sentences.en: And two years later, he sets off on foot for Rome, where he becomes a Jesuit.
sentences.zh: 两年后，他徒步前往罗马，在那里成为了一名耶稣会士。

sentences.en: And it's there in 1580 that he is recruited by Persons for the mission to England.
sentences.zh: 1580年，他在那里被珀森斯招募，参加前往英格兰的传教任务。

sentences.en: And actually, Campion hadn't wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 实际上，坎皮恩并不想去。

sentences.en: He agreed with the Jesuit general that this was provocative to send the Jesuits into England.
sentences.zh: 他同意耶稣会总会长的看法，认为派遣耶稣会士进入英格兰是一种挑衅行为。

sentences.en: But, you know, he's taken his vow of obedience, so he has to go.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他已经发了服从誓言，所以他必须去。

sentences.en: And so off he sets.
sentences.zh: 于是他出发了。

sentences.en: And you might think that if they're going undercover into England, that Persons and Campion would,
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，如果他们要潜入英格兰，珀森斯和坎皮恩会……

sentences.en: as they head from Rome towards the Channel, that they'd be doing it in a kind of stealthy manner, a clandestine manner, but not a bit of it.
sentences.zh: 当他们从罗马前往海峡时，他们会以一种隐秘的方式，秘密地进行，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So Campion writes to his superior back in Rome, saying that they were being accompanied by something positively like a clamour, because everyone knows they're coming.
sentences.zh: 坎皮恩写信给罗马的上级，说他们此行伴随着一种近乎喧嚣的动静，因为大家都知道他们要来了。

sentences.en: They're massive celebrities.
sentences.zh: 他们是大名人。

sentences.en: And their mission is seen by Catholics as something heroic and thrilling.
sentences.zh: 他们的使命被天主教徒视为英雄般的壮举，令人振奋。

sentences.en: And so despite themselves, they are celebrities even before they have arrived in England.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他们自己并不想，但在抵达英格兰之前，他们就已经成了名人。

sentences.en: Reckless.
sentences.zh: 鲁莽。

sentences.en: It is reckless, but maybe also a kind of challenge to the Protestant establishment, that we are coming as priests.
sentences.zh: 这确实很鲁莽，但也可能是一种对新教体制的挑战，表明我们是以神职人员的身份前来的。

sentences.en: And neither Walsingham nor Burley have any doubt as to particularly Campion's capabilities.
sentences.zh: 沃尔辛厄姆和伯利对坎皮恩的能力毫无怀疑。

sentences.en: You know, we said he's intellectually brilliant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们说过他才华横溢。

sentences.en: He has this amazing personal magnetism.
sentences.zh: 他有一种惊人的个人魅力。

sentences.en: He's a very warm, charming man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常热情、迷人的人。

sentences.en: Everybody thinks this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都这么认为。

sentences.en: And also this incredible sense of conviction that is total, but not alienating in the way that a kind of fanatical conviction is.
sentences.zh: 而且他有一种绝对的信念感，但这种信念又不像狂热分子那样让人反感。

sentences.en: So he is very, he convinces people without seeming kind of swivel eyed.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常有说服力，他能说服别人，却不会显得像个疯子。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: He's a true believer, but he's not mad, which is an important distinction.
sentences.zh: 他是一个真正的信徒，但他并不疯狂，这是一个重要的区别。

sentences.en: You're not going to recoil from him in the street.
sentences.zh: 你不会在街上看到他就退避三舍。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So all these qualities, of course, just make him seem more dangerous to Walsingham.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些特质，当然只会让他在沃尔辛厄姆眼中显得更加危险。

sentences.en: And the fact that the Jesuits are coming to England at this specific moment in particular makes them seem sinister.
sentences.zh: 而且耶稣会士在此时此刻来到英格兰，更让他们显得居心叵测。

sentences.en: So in Ireland, remember that invasion force that had been sent with the Spanish soldiers?
sentences.zh: 在爱尔兰，还记得那支带着西班牙士兵的入侵部队吗？

sentences.en: They're still in the field and they've been swollen by Irish Catholic rebels who have flocked
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在战场上，并且得到了爱尔兰天主教叛军的增援，他们蜂拥而至……

sentences.en: to the, actually the banner specifically of the Pope, because an English papal nuncio has landed and is preaching holy war against the heretic Jezebel on the English throne.
sentences.zh: 实际上是聚集在教皇的旗帜下，因为一位英格兰教皇使节已经登陆，并正在宣扬针对英格兰王位上那位“异端耶洗别”的圣战。

sentences.en: And so to quote Jesse Childs in her wonderful prize winning book, God's Traitors, which is
sentences.zh: 引用杰西·柴尔兹在她那本精彩的获奖著作《上帝的叛徒》中的话，这本书……

sentences.en: all about the recusants in Elizabethan England, from the government's viewpoint, it looked very much as though campion and persons were papal Spanish agents bent on subversion, not
sentences.zh: 讲述了伊丽莎白时代英格兰的拒不奉教者，从政府的角度来看，坎皮恩和珀森斯看起来非常像是教皇和西班牙的代理人，一心想要进行颠覆，而不是……

sentences.en: conversion.
sentences.zh: 皈依。

sentences.en: The Jesuits say it's about conversion.
sentences.zh: 耶稣会士说这是为了皈依。

sentences.en: Walsingham and Burley say, no, this is subversion.
sentences.zh: 沃尔辛厄姆和伯利说，不，这是颠覆。

sentences.en: But they would be right to say that, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 但他们说得没错，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, conversion and subversion are the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，皈依和颠覆是一回事。

sentences.en: If you are a Protestant minister of Queen Elizabeth, indisputably.
sentences.zh: 如果你是伊丽莎白女王的新教大臣，那毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you are a Catholic priest, I think you could say, well, I'm doing God's will.
sentences.zh: 如果你是天主教神父，我想你可以说，好吧，我是在执行上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: But it's a fine distinction because the Pope has excommunicated the Queen.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种微妙的区别，因为教皇已经将女王逐出教会了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's surely the killer detail.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这绝对是致命的细节。

sentences.en: You are not wrong.
sentences.zh: 你说得没错。

sentences.en: And Campion keeps very quiet about this.
sentences.zh: 而坎皮恩对此保持沉默。

sentences.en: Because you cannot possibly say, oh, well, this is politically neutral.
sentences.zh: 因为你不可能说，哦，这在政治上是中立的。

sentences.en: We're just, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，你知道。

sentences.en: Dominic, you absolutely can.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你绝对可以这么说。

sentences.en: And they do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么说了。

sentences.en: They do say that.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么说了。

sentences.en: But people don't believe them.
sentences.zh: 但人们不相信他们。

sentences.en: Well, certainly the Protestant authorities don't believe them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，新教当局肯定不相信他们。

sentences.en: And I suspect quite a lot of the Catholics don't believe them either.
sentences.zh: 而且我怀疑很多天主教徒也不相信他们。

sentences.en: But this is what they are saying.
sentences.zh: 但这正是他们所说的。

sentences.en: So you can see how essentially there is a kind of ideological opposition.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，本质上存在一种意识形态的对立。

sentences.en: And you can see that the question of what is their motivation?
sentences.zh: 你可以看出，关于他们的动机是什么的问题？

sentences.en: Is it to convert or is it to subvert?
sentences.zh: 是为了皈依还是为了颠覆？

sentences.en: Is absolutely what is at stake in this whole episode.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是整个事件的关键所在。

sentences.en: Absolutely crucial.
sentences.zh: 绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: So they've arrived in the Channel Ports.
sentences.zh: 所以他们抵达了海峡港口。

sentences.en: Now they've got the problem of how do they get over.
sentences.zh: 现在他们面临如何过境的问题。

sentences.en: Persons is the first to make the crossing.
sentences.zh: 珀森斯是第一个过境的人。

sentences.en: And he sets out from Calais to Dover on the 16th of June, 1580.
sentences.zh: 他于1580年6月16日从加来出发前往多佛。

sentences.en: And he has adopted a policy of wildly extravagant disguise.
sentences.zh: 他采取了一种极其夸张的伪装策略。

sentences.en: So he's dressed up as a kind of blood and thunder mercenary.
sentences.zh: 他打扮成一个粗鲁狂暴的雇佣兵。

sentences.en: He's got a leather coat that's trimmed with gold braid.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件镶有金边的皮大衣。

sentences.en: He's got a feather in his cap.
sentences.zh: 他的帽子上插着羽毛。

sentences.en: Massively fanboy.
sentences.zh: 简直是个狂热粉丝。

sentences.en: And I think he's just a natural ham.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他天生就是个戏精。

sentences.en: It's a good disguise, though.
sentences.zh: 不过这伪装确实不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really good disguise.
sentences.zh: 是的，这伪装真的很棒。

sentences.en: Because, you know, he's described by a Catholic as being such a peacock, such a swaggerer.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，他被一位天主教徒形容为像只孔雀，像个招摇过市的人。

sentences.en: And so no one thinks for a minute that he could possibly be a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以没人会想到他竟然可能是个神父。

sentences.en: And so he crosses with no problem at all.
sentences.zh: 于是他顺利地过境了。

sentences.en: Then Campion follows a week later.
sentences.zh: 一周后，坎皮恩紧随其后。

sentences.en: And he's disguised himself as a jeweler from Dublin.
sentences.zh: 他伪装成一个来自都柏林的珠宝商。

sentences.en: Because, of course, he'd spent time in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 因为他确实在都柏林待过。

sentences.en: So he's familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 所以他很熟悉那里。

sentences.en: And he gets stopped because he resembles William Allen's brother, who had been on Sled's list that he'd handed over to Walsingham.
sentences.zh: 但他被拦下了，因为他长得像威廉·艾伦的兄弟，而那个人在斯莱德交给沃尔辛厄姆的名单上。

sentences.en: And so he does get apprehended.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实被逮捕了。

sentences.en: And for reasons that aren't entirely clear, they don't keep him.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种不完全清楚的原因，他们没有扣留他。

sentences.en: So he manages to carry on from Dover.
sentences.zh: 所以他设法从多佛继续前行。

sentences.en: And he arrives in London, where he rendezvouses with Persons.
sentences.zh: 他抵达了伦敦，并在那里与珀森斯会合。

sentences.en: And Persons and Campion, for the next few weeks, are then touring safe houses across the capital.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几周，珀森斯和坎皮恩一直在首都各处的安全屋巡回。

sentences.en: And they're preaching.
sentences.zh: 他们进行布道。

sentences.en: And they're celebrating mass.
sentences.zh: 他们举行弥撒。

sentences.en: And they're hosting conferences with leading English Catholics, who are overjoyed to have these two very charismatic figures directly from the Pope in London.
sentences.zh: 他们与英格兰的主要天主教徒举行会议，这些天主教徒非常高兴能见到这两位直接来自教皇的魅力人物出现在伦敦。

sentences.en: And Campion, you know, he understands, Dominic, where Walsingham and you are coming from.
sentences.zh: 坎皮恩，你知道，多米尼克，他理解你和沃尔辛厄姆的立场。

sentences.en: He knows that he is being accused of treason.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己被指控犯有叛国罪。

sentences.en: And so he writes a formal letter explicitly denying this charge and insisting that he's come only, and I quote, to preach the gospel, to minister the sacraments,
sentences.zh: 所以他写了一封正式信件，明确否认这一指控，并坚称他来此只是为了，引用他的话，“宣扬福音，施行圣礼，教导平民，感化罪人，驳斥谬误”。

sentences.en: to instruct the simple, to reform sinners, to confute errors.
sentences.zh: 他给其他天主教徒的指示是：如果我被捕，就把这封信交给枢密院，让他们读一读，看看我的动机是什么。

sentences.en: And his instructions to his fellow Catholics are, should I be captured, then send this letter to the Privy Council so that they can read and see what my motivation is.
sentences.zh: 这封信的问题在于它写得太出色了。

sentences.en: The problem with this is that it's a brilliantly well-written letter.
sentences.zh: 我是说，坎皮恩所做的一切都很出色。

sentences.en: I mean, everything Campion does is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以天主教徒读了之后觉得，哦，这太棒了。

sentences.en: And so Catholics read it and they go, oh, this is great.
sentences.zh: 我们应该分享它。

sentences.en: We should share it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始抄写它。

sentences.en: And so they start copying it.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，它落入了沃尔辛厄姆特工的手中。

sentences.en: And so inevitably it falls into the hands of Walsingham's agents.
sentences.zh: 对英格兰的天主教徒来说，这封信是一个伟大的集结号。

sentences.en: To English Catholics, this letter is a great rallying cry.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得它非常感人且富有启发性。

sentences.en: They find it very moving and inspirational.
sentences.zh: 但对沃尔辛厄姆和更广泛的新教当局来说，这封信一点也不让人放心。

sentences.en: But to Walsingham and to the Protestant authorities more generally, this letter is not reassuring in the slighteSt.
sentences.zh: 它看起来是一种极其可怕的挑衅。

sentences.en: It seems a really terrifying provocation.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出原因。

sentences.en: And you can see why.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是坎皮恩所写的。

sentences.en: So this is also what Campion has written.
sentences.zh: 代价已计算。

sentences.en: The expense is reckoned.
sentences.zh: 事业已开始。

sentences.en: The enterprise is begun.
sentences.zh: 这是上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: It is of God.
sentences.zh: 不可阻挡。

sentences.en: It cannot be withstood.
sentences.zh: 信仰就是这样播下的。

sentences.en: So the faith was planted.
sentences.zh: 所以它必须被恢复。

sentences.en: So it must be restored.
sentences.zh: 你如何恢复它？

sentences.en: And how do you restore it?
sentences.zh: 通过除掉那个新教的耶洗别，把天主教的苏格兰女王扶上王位来恢复它。

sentences.en: You restore it by getting rid of the Protestant Jezebel and planting the Catholic Queen of Scots on the throne.
sentences.zh: 所以不出所料，在新教徒中，这封信很快就臭名昭著了。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, among Protestants, the letter is very soon notorious.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“坎皮恩的吹嘘”。

sentences.en: And they call it Campion's brag.
sentences.zh: 你觉得这不公平吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that's unfair?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，我是说，他什么也没说，只是读了读。

sentences.en: Do you think, I mean, he's not saying anything, just reading it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当然，你可以说这其中有一种意识形态的傲慢。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, there's a sort of, you might say there's kind of ideological arrogance to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是……

sentences.en: You know, we are.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他是个耶稣会士。

sentences.en: Well, he's a Jesuit.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说。

sentences.en: But, I mean.
sentences.zh: 我想，意识形态的傲慢正是成为某种宗教突击部队成员的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: Ideological arrogance is the whole point of being, I suppose, a kind of, you know, part of a religious shock force.
sentences.zh: 但我很惊讶他们竟然被它激怒到这种程度。

sentences.en: But I'm surprised that they're so provoked by it.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为他曾经是他们自己人。

sentences.en: I think it's because he was one of their own.
sentences.zh: 他用牛津受过教育的新教徒的风格写作，但他却把他们的武器对准了他们自己。

sentences.en: He's writing in the style of an Oxford educated Protestant, but he's turning their weapons against them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，再次类比一下剑桥叛徒事件，

sentences.en: I mean, again, you know, to draw the analogy with the Cambridge traitors,
sentences.zh: 让英国体制感到震惊的是，那些上过体面大学、属于圣詹姆斯俱乐部的人，

sentences.en: that's what's kind of shocking to the British establishment was that chaps who'd been to decent colleges and belong to clubs in St. James's.
sentences.zh: 竟然一直在为共产党工作。

sentences.en: And had been working for the communists.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为其中有这个因素，这封信写得实在是太好了。

sentences.en: And so I think there's an element of that, that this is a very, very well-written letter.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they know that Campion is unbelievably smart.
sentences.zh: 他们都知道坎皮恩聪明得不可思议。

sentences.en: And therefore, he, you know, they can read between the lines.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们能读懂言外之意。

sentences.en: They know what he's getting at.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他想表达什么。

sentences.en: And you compared him with the Cambridge traitors.
sentences.zh: 你把他和剑桥的叛徒们相提并论。

sentences.en: I mean, he acquires this sort of, I don't know, Kim Philby style reputation, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他获得了一种，我不知道该怎么说，类似金·菲尔比那样的名声，不是吗？

sentences.en: As a man who is, there's a kind of charisma to a sort of, you know, that fascinates his enemies as much as his adherents.
sentences.zh: 作为一个男人，他身上有一种魅力，你知道，这种魅力既吸引了他的敌人，也吸引了他的追随者。

sentences.en: I mean, Kim Philby is an evil man who portrayed lots of people to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 我是说，金·菲尔比是个邪恶的人，他把许多人出卖给了死神。

sentences.en: Campion is not doing that.
sentences.zh: 坎皮恩并没有那样做。

sentences.en: Campion is a very brave, committed, heroic man, I think, who absolutely believes what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 我认为坎皮恩是一个非常勇敢、坚定、英雄般的人物，他绝对相信自己所做的一切。

sentences.en: But he has a similar grip on the imagination that somebody like Philby had.
sentences.zh: 但他对人们想象力的掌控力，和菲尔比那样的人很像。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're saying he's very charismatic, then yes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你是说他很有魅力，那确实如此。

sentences.en: But he becomes a hero to Catholics because they see him, which I think he is, as a principled and heroic man who is touring.
sentences.zh: 但他成了天主教徒心目中的英雄，因为他们视他为一位原则坚定、英勇无畏的巡回传教士，我觉得他确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, he leaves London.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他离开了伦敦。

sentences.en: He tours Berkshire, Oxfordshire, Northamptonshire, so kind of the countryside.
sentences.zh: 他在伯克郡、牛津郡、北安普敦郡巡回传教，也就是在乡间。

sentences.en: He's preaching in barns.
sentences.zh: 他在谷仓里讲道。

sentences.en: And he's attracting ever-swelling congregations.
sentences.zh: 而且他的信众越来越多。

sentences.en: You know, he has a touch of the starduSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他身上有一种明星气质。

sentences.en: People want to come and hear him.
sentences.zh: 人们都想来听他讲道。

sentences.en: And undoubtedly, you know, he is getting converts.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，你知道，他正在争取皈依者。

sentences.en: And he's offering reassurance to Catholics who've been oppressed for a decade and a half now.
sentences.zh: 他为那些已经被压迫了十五年的天主教徒提供了慰藉。

sentences.en: And, of course, he's always on the move.
sentences.zh: 当然，他总是处于奔波之中。

sentences.en: He's always having to put on disguises which Campion himself regards as ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 他总是不得不乔装打扮，而坎皮恩本人觉得这很荒谬。

sentences.en: But, you know, for months and months, he's not caught.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，几个月过去了，他都没有被抓到。

sentences.en: And the whole Protestant spy agency are looking out for him.
sentences.zh: 而整个新教间谍机构都在搜捕他。

sentences.en: So that also adds to his kind of glamour, I think, the sense of him as, you know, a kind of secret agent as well as a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这也增加了他身上那种魅力，我想，那种既是秘密特工又是牧师的感觉。

sentences.en: And then on the 27th of June, 1581, so by this point, he's been there, you know, almost a year.
sentences.zh: 然后是在1581年6月27日，到这个时候，你知道，他已经在那里待了快一年了。

sentences.en: He throws down a very dramatic gauntlet by having an open challenge to the Queen printed and distributed across Oxford.
sentences.zh: 他抛出了一份极具戏剧性的挑战书，在牛津各地印刷并散发，公开向女王叫板。

sentences.en: And again, he is kind of tweaking the nose of the Protestant establishment.
sentences.zh: 他再次戏弄了新教当局。

sentences.en: So he writes in this pamphlet, listen, Elizabeth, mighty Queen, the prophet in speaking to thee is teaching thee thy duty.
sentences.zh: 他在小册子里写道：听着，伊丽莎白，强大的女王，向你传达神谕的先知是在教导你应尽的职责。

sentences.en: That is bound to seem provocative, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，这注定会被视为挑衅。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: To people like Walsingham.
sentences.zh: 对沃尔辛厄姆那样的人来说。

sentences.en: And so Walsingham says, come on, this is going beyond a joke.
sentences.zh: 所以沃尔辛厄姆说，得了吧，这简直是胡闹。

sentences.en: We have to get this guy.
sentences.zh: 我们必须抓住这家伙。

sentences.en: And it's clear by now that he is starting to kind of leave a trail.
sentences.zh: 很明显，到目前为止，他已经开始留下蛛丝马迹了。

sentences.en: And he's captured three weeks later on the 17th of July at a requisite house called Lifford Grange in Berkshire.
sentences.zh: 三周后的7月17日，他在伯克郡一个叫利福德庄园的必要住所被捕了。

sentences.en: And actually, the people who are coming to who find him were not specifically looking for him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那些找到他的人并不是专门来找他的。

sentences.en: They were looking for other priests.
sentences.zh: 他们是在找其他牧师。

sentences.en: But he is found after a two day search hiding in a priest hole with these two other priests.
sentences.zh: 但在两天的搜查后，他被发现和另外两名牧师一起躲在牧师藏身处。

sentences.en: And the guy who has led them there is a very sinister figure called George Eliot.
sentences.zh: 带他们去那里的那个人是一个非常阴险的人物，叫乔治·艾略特。

sentences.en: So he's the spy catcher.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个间谍捕手。

sentences.en: And he's a Catholic apostate who, you know, as is the way so often with apostates, are keen to he's keen to prove himself more Protestant than the Protestants.
sentences.zh: 他是一个天主教叛教者，你知道，正如叛教者常有的那样，他急于证明自己比新教徒更像新教徒。

sentences.en: And he has been playing on the Privy Council's paranoia.
sentences.zh: 他一直在利用枢密院的偏执心理。

sentences.en: You know, he's been really bigging up all the stuff about plots and things funded by the Pope, assassinations of Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一直在大肆渲染关于阴谋、教皇资助以及暗杀伊丽莎白之类的事情。

sentences.en: I think coming up with material that wasn't actually true.
sentences.zh: 我想他编造了一些根本不是事实的材料。

sentences.en: And he very shrewdly tells Burley and Walsingham that they're in line to be murdered as well.
sentences.zh: 他非常精明地告诉伯利和沃尔辛厄姆，他们也在被暗杀的名单上。

sentences.en: So that kind of adds to that sense of urgency in trying to find these priests.
sentences.zh: 这增加了寻找这些牧师的紧迫感。

sentences.en: And so when Campion is brought out from the priest hole, you know, he is not treated well, which is what you would expect.
sentences.zh: 所以当坎皮恩从牧师藏身处被带出来时，你知道，他没有受到善待，这也是意料之中的。

sentences.en: So he's his elbows are tied behind him.
sentences.zh: 他的手肘被反绑在身后。

sentences.en: He's plonked on a horse.
sentences.zh: 他被扔到马背上。

sentences.en: A sign is pinned to his hat, which reads Campion, the seditious Jesuit.
sentences.zh: 他的帽子上别着一个牌子，上面写着：坎皮恩，煽动叛乱的耶稣会士。

sentences.en: And he is led straight to the Tower of London, where he is locked up in this hideous cell called Little E's, which is a joke because you can neither stretch nor rise to your feet.
sentences.zh: 他被直接带到伦敦塔，关进了一个叫“小E”的恐怖牢房，这很讽刺，因为你在里面既不能伸展身体，也不能站起来。

sentences.en: So he spends three days there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里待了三天。

sentences.en: It must have been agony.
sentences.zh: 那一定非常痛苦。

sentences.en: But Little E's is not to be the worst because the rack is waiting.
sentences.zh: 但“小E”还不是最糟糕的，因为刑架还在等着他。

sentences.en: And people may be wondering, well, you know, what's the status of torture in England at this time?
sentences.zh: 人们可能想知道，当时英国的酷刑状况如何？

sentences.en: Torture is illegal.
sentences.zh: 酷刑是非法的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, Walsingham is convinced that it has to be applied.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，沃尔辛厄姆确信必须使用酷刑。

sentences.en: So he had written to Burley in 1575, without torture, I know we shall not prevail.
sentences.zh: 所以他在1575年写信给伯利说：没有酷刑，我知道我们无法获胜。

sentences.en: Golly, very war on terror.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这简直就是反恐战争。

sentences.en: Kind of Dick Cheney, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有点像迪克·切尼，不是吗？

sentences.en: What was it?
sentences.zh: 那叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Enhanced interrogation techniques.
sentences.zh: 强化审讯技术。

sentences.en: It's a no-brainer.
sentences.zh: 这显而易见。

sentences.en: So I think for Walsingham, it's a no-brainer.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对沃尔辛厄姆来说，这显而易见。

sentences.en: So Campion, in his brag, that letter he'd written that was meant to be private, which had gone viral,
sentences.zh: 所以坎皮恩，在他那份本应保密却意外流传开来的“吹嘘信”中，

sentences.en: he had declared his defiance of Elizabeth's judicial authorities by directly name-checking the prospect of torture.
sentences.zh: 他直接点名提到了酷刑的可能性，以此表达对伊丽莎白司法当局的蔑视。

sentences.en: So he'd said, while we have a man left to enjoy your Tyburn, where people hang, or to be racked with torments, or to be consumed with your prisons, you know, we will keep coming.
sentences.zh: 他说：只要我们还有人能享受你们的泰伯恩刑场（人们被绞死的地方），或者被酷刑折磨，或者被你们的监狱吞噬，你知道，我们还是会不断涌现。

sentences.en: And he was right to dread what the Protestant authorities would do, because in the Tower, he is repeatedly racked.
sentences.zh: 他害怕新教当局会对他做什么，这是对的，因为在伦敦塔，他反复遭受刑架折磨。

sentences.en: And it's so brutal that he loses the use of his pen hand.
sentences.zh: 这太残忍了，以至于他失去了写字的手的功能。

sentences.en: So people may remember that Guy Fawkes, you know, you can look at his signature before and after he's been racked.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得盖伊·福克斯，你知道，你可以看看他受刑前后的签名。

sentences.en: Campion has it so badly that he can't even sign a paper.
sentences.zh: 坎皮恩受到的折磨太严重了，他甚至无法签署文件。

sentences.en: And when he's not being tortured, he's being subjected to various inquiries.
sentences.zh: 当他不被折磨时，他还要接受各种审讯。

sentences.en: So there's a judicial inquiry led by Robert Beale.
sentences.zh: 有一个由罗伯特·比尔领导的司法调查。

sentences.en: There's a big theological debate, which is staged in the parish church of the Tower.
sentences.zh: 还有一场在伦敦塔教区教堂举行的大型神学辩论。

sentences.en: And Campion is only allowed the Bible, so he's not allowed any other books, no other reference books.
sentences.zh: 坎皮恩只被允许使用圣经，不允许使用任何其他书籍，没有其他参考书。

sentences.en: And then there's a public trial is staged in Westminster Hall in November 1581.
sentences.zh: 然后是在1581年11月在威斯敏斯特大厅举行的公开审判。

sentences.en: And throughout all these processes, the core argument is the one that we were talking about earlier.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些过程中，核心论点就是我们之前讨论过的那个。

sentences.en: Is his mission a pastoral one or is it blatant treason?
sentences.zh: 他的使命是牧灵工作，还是公然的叛国罪？

sentences.en: And this is, you know, they just keep going over and over and over it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们就是不断地重复讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: And there's never really any doubt as to what the verdict is going to be.
sentences.zh: 而且对于判决结果，从来没有任何疑问。

sentences.en: So on the 20th of November, Campion is convicted, not of heresy, not of any crime of conscience,
sentences.zh: 所以11月20日，坎皮恩被定罪，不是因为异端，也不是因为任何良心罪，

sentences.en: but as an offender against a statute against treason that had been passed in the reign of Edward III 220 years before.
sentences.zh: 而是作为一个违反了220年前爱德华三世统治时期通过的叛国罪法规的罪犯。

sentences.en: So he is convicted as a traitor.
sentences.zh: 所以他被定为叛国罪。

sentences.en: And on the 1st of December, he suffers the death of a traitor.
sentences.zh: 12月1日，他遭受了叛国者的死刑。

sentences.en: So he is lashed onto a hurdle.
sentences.zh: 他被绑在木架上。

sentences.en: He is taken from his prison to Tyburn, which is now Marble Arch in London, but was the traditional place for executions.
sentences.zh: 他从监狱被带到泰伯恩，也就是现在伦敦的大理石拱门，那是传统的行刑地点。

sentences.en: And there he suffers the hideous, hideous death of a traitor.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他遭受了叛国者那种极其恐怖的死刑。

sentences.en: So he's hanged until he is almost dead.
sentences.zh: 他被绞到快要断气。

sentences.en: He's then cut down.
sentences.zh: 然后被放下来。

sentences.en: He is still alive as his bowels and his genitals are cut off and pulled out and burnt in front of him.
sentences.zh: 在他还活着的时候，他的肠子和生殖器被割掉、拉出，并在他面前焚烧。

sentences.en: And then when he's dead, his body is quartered and the various quarters are dispatched to gateways around London.
sentences.zh: 等他死后，他的尸体被肢解，各部分被送到伦敦各处的城门口。

sentences.en: And Walsingham and Burley and the Privy Council take a very, very grim satisfaction in Campion's fate because it draws what seems to be a line under what had been a very grim year.
sentences.zh: 沃尔辛厄姆、伯利和枢密院对坎皮恩的下场感到非常、非常阴暗的满足，因为它似乎为这极其阴暗的一年画上了一个句号。

sentences.en: So first, that rebellion in Ireland, we talked about the Spanish troops, the papal nuncio, that has been suppressed.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们谈到的爱尔兰叛乱，西班牙军队，教皇使节，这些都已经被镇压了。

sentences.en: It took place at a place called Smurwick in County Kerry, and all the Spanish troops had been satisfyingly massacred.
sentences.zh: 它发生在凯里郡一个叫斯默威克的地方，所有的西班牙军队都被令人满意地屠杀了。

sentences.en: And now the most dangerous papist agent that has been sent to England under Elizabeth has been captured, convicted and killed.
sentences.zh: 现在，伊丽莎白统治下派往英国的最危险的教皇特工已经被捕、定罪并处决了。

sentences.en: And of course, Persons is still on the scene, but he manages to to slip away.
sentences.zh: 当然，帕森斯还在现场，但他设法溜走了。

sentences.en: And the flow of priests does continue into the country for the rest of Elizabeth's reign.
sentences.zh: 在伊丽莎白统治的余下时间里，牧师流入国内的情况确实还在继续。

sentences.en: But I think that Walsingham and his men now feel that they have the measure of what is going on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为沃尔辛厄姆和他的手下现在觉得他们已经掌握了局势。

sentences.en: And over the course of Elizabeth's reign, 471 priests will end up being captured and 116 of these will be executed.
sentences.zh: 在伊丽莎白统治期间，最终有471名牧师被捕，其中116人被处决。

sentences.en: And the reason that the numbers are so high is because neither side is willing to abandon its respective strategy.
sentences.zh: 人数如此之高的原因是双方都不愿放弃各自的策略。

sentences.en: Because both sides, I think, feel that the benefits they secure from what they're doing outweighs the costs.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为双方都觉得他们从所作所为中获得的利益超过了成本。

sentences.en: So for Walsingham's men, they are stopping the proselytization of potential Catholics.
sentences.zh: 对沃尔辛厄姆的人来说，他们是在阻止潜在天主教徒的皈依。

sentences.en: It's destroying a foreign-funded campaign of subversion.
sentences.zh: 这摧毁了一场由外国资助的颠覆运动。

sentences.en: For the Catholic priests, their deaths enshrines them as martyrs and gives them what Protestants had been given under Mary Tudor.
sentences.zh: 对天主教牧师来说，他们的死亡使他们成为殉道者，并赋予了他们新教徒在玛丽·都铎统治下所拥有的东西。

sentences.en: So to this day, Edward Campion and a lot of the Catholic priests who were executed under Elizabeth, they're saints.
sentences.zh: 所以直到今天，爱德华·坎皮恩和许多在伊丽莎白统治下被处决的天主教牧师，他们都是圣人。

sentences.en: They kind of give their names to rooms in Catholic schools and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们以自己的名字命名天主教学校的房间之类的东西。

sentences.en: But the consequence for the climate in Elizabethan England is undoubtedly to generate a sense of paranoia, as you always do when there's a kind of espionage war going on.
sentences.zh: 但这对伊丽莎白时代英国气候的影响，无疑是产生了一种偏执感，就像任何时候发生间谍战时一样。

sentences.en: And because this is a specifically Christian espionage war, it gives people on both sides, Catholics and Protestants,
sentences.zh: 而且因为这是一场特殊的基督教间谍战，它让双方的人，无论是天主教徒还是新教徒，

sentences.en: a sense that they're living in the shadow of a kind of great cosmic drama.
sentences.zh: 都感觉到他们生活在某种宏大宇宙戏剧的阴影之下。

sentences.en: But a drama that's not just playing out in the shadows, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但这场戏剧不仅仅是在阴影中上演，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's not just a story about spies and back rooms and priest holes and double agents, is it?
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个关于间谍、密室、牧师藏身处和双重间谍的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's also a story of swashbuckling sea dogs.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个关于海上冒险家的故事。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's what we'll be turning to next time.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们下次要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So in the next episode, from the coast of California to the Straits of Magellan,
sentences.zh: 所以下一集，从加利福尼亚海岸到麦哲伦海峡，

sentences.en: we will be venturing onto the Marine Front in the ideological struggle between Protestantism and Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 我们将冒险进入新教与天主教意识形态斗争的海上阵线。

sentences.en: And in particular, we will be heading onto the Pacific Ocean with one of the greatest figures of the Elizabethan age, not a controversial figure these days,
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们将与伊丽莎白时代最伟大的人物之一一起前往太平洋，他现在可不是一个有争议的人物，

sentences.en: and that is Sir Francis Drake.
sentences.zh: 那就是弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士。

sentences.en: So loads of excitement, loads of rough action, loads of swashbuckling swordplay to come next time.
sentences.zh: 所以下次会有很多刺激、很多激烈的行动、很多精彩的剑术表演。

sentences.en: Now, if you remember the Restless History Club, you may well be on the Pacific Ocean as we speak.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你还记得“不安的历史俱乐部”，你现在可能就在太平洋上。

sentences.en: You may not even be listening to this, because you may be already listening to that episode right now, because you can, of course, because you get all the episodes early.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能没在听这一集，因为你可能已经在听那一集了，因为你可以，当然，因为你可以提前收听所有剧集。

sentences.en: If you're not a member of the Restless History Club and you'd like to be part of our own shadowy cabal of sinister conspirators,
sentences.zh: 如果你不是“不安的历史俱乐部”的成员，并且想加入我们自己阴暗的邪恶阴谋家集团，

sentences.en: then you just need to head to therestishistory.com to sign up.
sentences.zh: 那么你只需要前往 therestishistory.com 注册即可。

sentences.en: And, of course, that's the only way you'll get the host of unbelievable benefits.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是你获得大量难以置信的福利的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And there are other ways to sign up, but only through the website, therestishistory.com, do you get the cornucopia of delights that we offer our members.
sentences.zh: 还有其他注册方式，但只有通过网站 therestishistory.com，你才能获得我们为会员提供的丰厚礼品。

sentences.en: And, of course, the other thing you can do is to sign up to our free newsletter, and there you get all kinds of absolutely riveting articles, interviews, book extracts, and more.
sentences.zh: 当然，你还可以做的一件事是订阅我们的免费时事通讯，在那里你可以获得各种绝对引人入胜的文章、采访、书籍摘录等等。

sentences.en: We're also doing a live show, aren't we, about the ultimate Victorian adventure, which is the Abyssinian Expedition of 1868.
sentences.zh: 我们还要举办一场现场演出，不是吗？关于终极的维多利亚时代冒险，也就是1868年的阿比西尼亚远征。

sentences.en: All kicked off when the Abyssinian Emperor wrote a letter to Queen Victoria, and she neglected to reply.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于阿比西尼亚皇帝写信给维多利亚女王，而她忽略了回复。

sentences.en: He got in a massive strop, and chaos ensued.
sentences.zh: 他大发雷霆，随后陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's absolutely an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是一个令人惊叹的故事。

sentences.en: It's one of the most lurid, implausible, and entertaining of all 19th century imperial adventures.
sentences.zh: 这是19世纪所有帝国冒险中最耸人听闻、最不可思议且最有趣的故事之一。

sentences.en: So I'm really looking forward to the show.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常期待这场演出。

sentences.en: It's very Flashman, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常有《弗莱什曼》的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's a Flashman book about it, Flashman on the March.
sentences.zh: 有一本关于它的《弗莱什曼》书，《弗莱什曼进军》。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the ideal Flashman story if you like Flashman.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你喜欢《弗莱什曼》，这是理想的《弗莱什曼》故事。

sentences.en: And even if you don't, it's still brilliant.
sentences.zh: 即使你不喜欢，它依然非常精彩。

sentences.en: Anyway, that is at the South Bank in London on Friday the 4th of September, and you can get tickets once again at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 总之，演出将于9月4日星期五在伦敦南岸举行，你可以再次在 therestishistory.com 购票。

sentences.en: I think you should just bookmark therestishistory.com and buy everything it's got to offer.
sentences.zh: 我认为你应该把 therestishistory.com 加入书签，并购买它所提供的一切。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, we'll be back next time with Sir Francis Drake.
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这个重磅消息，我们下次将带着弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士回来。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
